transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Lee (Sentinel Health - Head of MLOps), Carlos Ramirez (Infra), Priya Shah (Security)

Summary:
Quick sync on the Redwood Private (VPC) pilot: network routing issues observed last week, a kernel/driver mismatch causing GPU instability on one node, tuning results from caching/batching changes, and next steps for an on-prem upgrade window. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Network routing / NAT / peering troubleshooting
- Kernel/CUDA driver mismatch and planned upgrade
- Performance tuning: batching / KV cache behavior for our workload
- Security: KMS integration, audit logs, SSO
- Next steps and pilot timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, happy Friday. we, we wanted to run through the items from the ticket — the routing bits and then the perf numbers that Samir pulled together. Dana, you good to start?

[00:12] Dana: Yeah thanks, Ava. Quick recap — on Tuesday we saw intermittent 5xxs when routing requests to the private endpoints, looks like it was hitting a single node then the requests timed out. we did a quick restart and it recovered but we're seeing packets being SNATed unexpectedly.

[00:28] Carlos: Yeah I dug in — looks like the NAT gateway rules in the staging VPC were applied to the wrong subnet. we have two private subnets; the route table got associated with subnet-b instead of subnet-a, so some egress was going via the public NAT, causing sessions to break with the bastion/ssh breakage too.

[00:45] Samir: Ok so that explains the ephemeral IP translation; Redwood's routing policy expects the worker nodes to maintain consistent source IP for the inference connections so the stateful routing and the KV cache affinity can stick. If SNAT flips the source, the sticky routing can send requests to a node with cold KV cache which spikes latency and sometimes the node sees tokenized health-checks and throws a 502.

[01:05] Dana: Right, the symptom we saw was higher p95 and occasional 500s, mostly on longer context runs. we had a follow-up where one node threw out-of-memory on the KV cache and restarted.

[01:20] Samir: We looked at the logs — that restart correlated with a CUDA driver mismatch after the host kernel auto-updated in the datacenter. the kernel/driver combo got out of supported bounds for the quantized runtime, so one node had slower kernels and memory accounting bugs.

[01:38] Carlos: We actually saw the host upgrade happen overnight — turns out our patch policy allowed a minor kernel bump. we should have pinned that in the pilot cluster but, hindsight.

[01:48] Priya: From security perspective, the unexpected egress is a concern — we need flow logs and audit trails. also want to confirm that KMS calls from the Redwood agent are going through our private endpoints and not egressing to public key services.

[02:05] Ava: Understood. Actionable items there — Carlos to send SOC2/VPC flow logs and the sg rules. we also will share a network diagram that shows recommended route table associations and NAT placement; that should avoid the SNAT flip we observed.

[02:18] Dana: Sounds good. quick question on KMS — we tested customer-managed keys earlier, Samir, is there any outbound call to Redwood infra?

[02:27] Samir: No, for Private the control plane negotiates key exchange in the customer VPC if you use the on-prem key proxy; there's a mode where keys are never sent to Redwood and CMKs are used via an AWS KMS endpoint in your account. we do need the right IAM role and the bastion to reach the KMS endpoint, or use a private link. If that path is misconfigured we'll see requests fail during initialization.

[02:50] Carlos: We planned a PrivateLink but haven't wired it for KMS yet. Priya, that's on your list right?

[02:56] Priya: Yep, I'll verify the key policy and confirm the private link requirement; also need to schedule rotation windows.

[03:06] Ava: Ok shifting to perf — Samir you ran the two baseline sets after the batching changes?

[03:12] Samir: Yeah so we updated the batcher config to increase max_batch_size from 8 to 12 for the high-throughput route and enabled prefix KV caching for common preambles. Overall tokens/sec improved 18% on 2k-context workloads, p95 dropped by ~35ms, but for 8k-context the memory pressure was higher and we saw a few OOMs on the smaller instance class.

[03:39] Dana: That's consistent with what we saw in our smoke tests — short requests faster, but long-context runs fail occasionally. What instance classes are those OOM nodes?

[03:47] Samir: The failing ones were on g4dn-style 1x GPUs with 16GB; for 8k context you want at least 40GB or quantized 8-bit models on 24GB with kernel patches. Redwood's recommendation is either a bigger instance or apply model quantization to reduce KV memory.

[04:03] Carlos: We're constrained on budget for the pilot so swapping instance types isn't ideal. can we try more aggressive quantization? any accuracy hit we should expect?

[04:12] Samir: We can do dynamic quantization and a 4-bit or 8-bit recipe — based on the eval set you shared, we saw negligible quality regression (<1.5% ROUGE drop) with the 8-bit path, but 4-bit needs a quick eval on your prompts. I'll run a validation sweep.

[04:30] Dana: Please run it on our longer prompts, that's where we care most.

[04:35] Samir: Will do. Also ran a quick KV cache eviction tune — lowered TTL for conversation prefix to reduce memory and increased eviction aggressiveness for inactive sessions. that cut the OOM events in half for mid-size nodes.

[04:52] Priya: We also want to confirm audit logs — can Redwood push agent logs to our S3 bucket or do we need to pull them?

[04:59] Ava: Redwood can forward logs via an SQS->S3 delivery or you can mount a fluentd collector. We'll include the runbook with both options.

[05:10] Dana: Good. Another item — we hit an intermittent TLS handshake failure between the control plane and the agent after the kernel bump. any idea?

[05:19] Samir: Likely the openssl library changed ABI after the host kernel update and the agent's bundled libcrypto had mismatch. we recommend pinning the agent container runtime and locking host libs or upgrading the agent to the latest shim which is ABI tolerant. We can push a hotfix to the agent tomorrow and coordinate a rolling restart, should be low-risk.

[05:42] Carlos: We prefer a maintenance window for restarts — can we do the rolling restarts during low traffic on 2026-07-10?

[05:49] Ava: Yes, we'll plan for a 2 hour window and provide a checklist. Samir, you'll coordinate the commit and the exact sequence?

[05:55] Samir: Yep, I'll prepare the steps and the rollback plan.

[06:00] Dana: One ask from product — when you run the 8k benchmark, include detailed token-level latency and breakdowns so we can see batching vs kernel time. also include traces for a few slow requests.

[06:12] Samir: Will include token-level breakdown and a per-request trace capture for three representative slow runs.

[06:20] Priya: For compliance, we need confirmation that we can enable RBAC and SSO for the console without sending PII to Redwood. also request data retention settings for logs.

[06:32] Ava: You can enable SSO via SAML and RBAC is configurable on the console; audit logs can be routed to your S3 and retained per your policy. we'll attach the security pack (SOC2, ISO certs) and the KMS integration doc after the call.

[06:44] Dana: Thanks. Any competitors mentioned during the internal review — we looked at Anthropic and Bedrock for hosted options but they don't match our need for on-prem private KMS.

[06:55] Ava: Right, that's one of the reasons you chose Private. ok quick recap of action items and owners...

[07:04] Ava: Carlos will send flow logs and SG rules by 2026-07-05; Priya will confirm KMS policy and rotation window by 2026-07-06; Samir will run the 8k perf sweep and quantization eval and share results by 2026-07-07; Ava to share network diagram and runbook by 2026-07-03; schedule maintenance for 2026-07-10 for rolling restarts.

[07:30] Dana: Sounds good. Anything else?

[07:33] Carlos: Just to note, we might need a quick escalated call if the perf run shows regressions — to decide on instance swap vs quantization.

[07:41] Samir: If needed we can run a cost vs perf spreadsheet to show tradeoffs; I can produce that.

[07:46] Ava: Great. thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the ticket with attachments and the runbook. end call.

[07:55] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription quality: some speaker labels may have been auto-assigned, occasional word swaps (e.g., SNAT/SNATed, KV cache abbreviations), times approximate.
